solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: City areas less urban, on reflection? Not entirely (8)

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read right to left
only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies inside it rather than using all of it

blocks.note: the letters run across the words: areaS LESS URBan

annotation.surface: A musing on whether some parts of a city feel less urban than others.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Not entirely' make it look like a remark about suburbs; the answer is lying backwards across the first three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Belgian capital is one of countless cities.

entries.clue: Newly organised soldiers also took charge (8)

annotation.surface: Soldiers being reorganised while also taking command.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Newly organised' looks like an anagram indicator for 'soldiers', but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a factory re-equipped with new tools is set up afresh, so the word stretches to any reorganisation.

entries.clue: Direct approach secures answer immediately (12)

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the outer phrase closes round the letter

blocks.note: a straight way = a direct approach
A = answer, as in Q and A

annotation.surface: Advice that a direct approach gets you an answer at once.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Direct approach' reads as a single idea in the surface, and it really does supply the outside of the answer, split by A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean without any delay.

entries.clue: Fatigue rising about heartless African from part of Africa (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, something rising goes upward, so the word is read from the bottom up
with the heart, the middle, cut out, only the two ends of the word are left

blocks.note: AFRICAN with its inside removed leaves A…N

annotation.surface: A tired African traveller from somewhere in Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: Eritrea is a country on the Red Sea coast in the Horn of Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective of origin: the Horn of Africa country Eritrea is the part of Africa meant.

entries.clue: Unseemly argument, perhaps over railway setting? (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed over another sits above it in the column

blocks.note: making a scene: a public row is one example

annotation.surface: A row that broke out over a railway line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags that an unseemly argument is only one kind of scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre sense: the painted backdrop on stage provides a play's setting.

entries.clue: Gym apparatus? Lands with head lowered (6)

indicators.note: the head of a down word is its top letter, and lowering it moves that letter further down the column

annotation.surface: A gymnast landing head down on the apparatus.
annotation.walkthrough: The S at the top of SHORES drops down to become the fourth letter; the question mark admits that 'apparatus' has to be read as plural.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: vaulting and pommel horses are two items of gym apparatus.

entries.clue: Author has to support good play (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever supports something is placed beneath it

blocks.note: the setter is the author, and 'I have' is written I'VE

annotation.surface: A writer backing a good stage play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' is not a drama but slack, the looseness in a rope or a steering wheel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of slack: a rope with some give has some play in it.

entries.clue: Right hand agitated my itch connected with pulse? (8)

indicators.note: something agitated is stirred up and shaken, so the letters lose their order

annotation.surface: A twitchy right hand, with an itch that throbs with the pulse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests the heartbeat, but here it is a musical beat.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical sense: a pulse is a regular beat, and music with one has rhythm.

entries.clue: Rather stupid, introducing bit of lamb into fish course (8)

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word is taken, its first letter
to introduce something is to bring it in, so the letter is put inside
the letter goes into the phrase that follows

blocks.note: a cod dish is a fish course

annotation.surface: A daft chef adding lamb to the fish course.
annotation.walkthrough: The L slots in straight after the C of COD DISH.
annotation.definitionFit: Built from a noun: a clod is a dolt, and -ish makes it 'rather' so.

entries.clue: Backed disturbances, but not over prison (4)

indicators.note: something backed has been moved backwards, so the word is read right to left
'not' excludes what comes next, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: O = over, in cricket scoring; this letter is removed

annotation.surface: Supporting prison riots, though not one over the prison itself.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone backing a riot; dropping the O from the reversed word is what matters.
annotation.definitionFit: Old criminal slang: to be 'in stir' is to be in prison.

entries.clue: Shock? The man isn’t so shocked (12)

indicators.note: a shocked thing is jolted out of place, so the letters are jolted into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone asks if something is a shock, and a man replies he isn't so shocked.
annotation.walkthrough: Definition and indicator are the same word in two forms, which makes the clue feel like a conversation rather than a recipe.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: great surprise is a kind of shock, which the question mark allows.

entries.clue: Having a reasonable salary suggests open-minded management primarily? (6-6)

indicators.note: in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of open-minded and management
the answer, read another way, points to these letters

annotation.surface: A comfortable salary as the sign of a broad-minded boss.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'the MIDDLE IN COME', and it gives OM, the middle of COME; the tail of the clue produces OM too.
annotation.definitionFit: A set phrase: a middle-income earner sits in the middle band of pay, a reasonable salary.

entries.clue: Badger turned up around trail beside rear of pasture (6)

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run backwards
going round, so the reversed word wraps around the next piece
the next piece is placed alongside, straight after
the rear of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A badger surfacing on a path by the back of a field.
annotation.walkthrough: The animal is really a verb: to badger is to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to plague someone with questions is to badger them.

entries.clue: What remains strange about side playing United? (8)

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, so the outer word encloses the rest
things at play move about freely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: U = United, as in football team names

annotation.surface: A strange question about a team playing against United.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' and 'United' look like two football teams in a fixture; both feed the same anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: residuum is the Latin-derived word for a residue, what is left over.

entries.clue: French writer recalled receiving money for working on newspaper? (7)

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the name is read backwards
a word receiving another takes it inside itself

annotation.surface: A French author paid for journalism, recalled years later.
annotation.walkthrough: Gide was a French novelist; the question mark admits that editing is only one way to work on a newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: editing is one of the jobs done on a newspaper.

entries.clue: Hour after the Spanish occasion is a late one (8)

indicators.note: the piece named first comes after the others in the answer

annotation.surface: A Spanish party that does not get going until the small hours.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'the eleventh hour', the last possible moment.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the eleventh hour is proverbially a late one, just before time runs out.

entries.clue: Spineless individual, American, about to follow associate of Capone? (7)

indicators.note: these pieces follow, coming after the gangster's companion

annotation.surface: A cowardly American hanging around after one of Al Capone's gang.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spineless' reads as cowardly, but the answer literally has no backbone.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading: molluscs are invertebrates, creatures with no spine at all.

entries.clue: Rock face banning English, one in Scottish town (8)

indicators.note: banning someone keeps them out, so that letter is removed
these letters are put in the next word, inside it

blocks.note: a side is a face, as of a cube
Oban, a port on Scotland's west coast

annotation.surface: A cliff face in a Scottish town where the English are barred.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock face' reads as a cliff; the definition is only 'Rock', and 'face' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: obsidian, a black volcanic glass, is one kind of rock.

entries.clue: Film star’s horse in pride of place here? (8)

definitions.text: horse in pride of place here?

blocks.clueFragment: horse in pride of place here?
blocks.note: a cryptic hint: where the top horse would be stabled

annotation.surface: A film star's prized racehorse kept in the best stable.
annotation.walkthrough: Split it as STALL ONE, the number one stall, which is where a horse in pride of place would be kept.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sylvester Stallone, of Rocky and Rambo, is a Hollywood film star.

entries.clue: Snake here has more than half twisted (7)

indicators.note: twisted round to face the other way, so those letters run backwards

blocks.note: only the first four of the seven letters, PRES, are turned

annotation.surface: A snake here, more than half coiled up.
annotation.walkthrough: Only PRES, just over half of the word, is turned; the rest stays put.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: serpent is the older, literary word for a snake.

entries.clue: Decline farewell involving capital of Wales or place nearby? (4,4)

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the two words take the letter in between them
the capital, the capital letter, is the first letter of the word

annotation.surface: A goodbye to Cardiff, or to a town close to it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Wales' pulls toward Cardiff, and the definition plays on that: the answer is a South Wales valley town not far from the capital.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic pointer: this South Wales town lies near Cardiff, the capital the clue has just raised.

entries.clue: Impassioned sporting body elevated game (6)

indicators.note: something elevated is raised up, so in a down clue its letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: FA, the Football Association, turned up
a game leg is a lame one

annotation.surface: A sports authority raising the profile of a passionate game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Game' is not a match here but the old adjective for an injured limb.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: someone aflame with passion is burning with it.

entries.clue: I run in circuits, going round curving course (6)

indicators.note: I and R are placed in the other word, inside it
the reversed word goes round the others, enclosing them

annotation.surface: A runner going round and round a winding track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circuits' does double duty in the surface as laps of the track, and that is exactly what it gives before being turned.
annotation.definitionFit: A shape word: a path that keeps winding round a centre follows a spiral.

entries.clue: Enclosed line in revised copy — editor in charge covering everything (12)

indicators.note: the line is put in the rearranged word, inside it
a revised text has been rewritten, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, as at the foot of a letter

annotation.surface: An editor's note on a revised proof with a line enclosed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enclosed' looks like a container indicator, but it is the letter-writing abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Built from encyclopedia: a work that covers every subject, so encyclopedic knowledge covers everything.

entries.clue: Pitch marker almost split (4)

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: cleft = split, less its final T

annotation.surface: A marker on a sports pitch that has nearly split.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is musical pitch.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical sense: the sign at the start of a stave marks which pitch each line stands for.

entries.clue: Wind player ducks end of piece after interruption of ‘Bravo’ (4)

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle, so the letter goes between the two Os
the end of a word is its last letter
the E comes after the rest

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks are O and O
Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A wind player ducking out of the end of a piece as the audience shouts bravo.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the instrument, but orchestras also call the player by the instrument's name, as in 'second oboe'.
annotation.definitionFit: A metonymy: in an orchestra a player is named for the instrument, so the second oboe is a person.

entries.clue: The control securing source of music in electronic instrument (8)

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it safely inside, so the rein closes round the letter
the source of something is where it begins, so the first letter

blocks.note: the + rein, a control on a horse

annotation.surface: A control on an electronic instrument that gets the music going.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is famously played without touch, the hands moving near two antennae, which makes 'control' a nice touch.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Russian-invented theremin was among the first electronic instruments.

entries.clue: Contract returned before finale from star fiddler (8)

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the word is read right to left
the finale is the ending, so the last letter of the word

blocks.note: to knit is to contract, draw together, as brows do; KNIT turned round

annotation.surface: A star violinist's contract, renewed just before the final concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fiddler' and 'star' suggest a violinist; the fiddler here is someone who fiddles with gadgets.
annotation.definitionFit: A second sense of fiddle: to fiddle about with a machine is to tinker with it.
